rules.name: WMIC remote XSL stylesheet (Astaroth-style)
rules.description: wmic.exe invoked with /format: pointing at a remote URL, a loading technique publicly documented for Astaroth (Guildma) chains in Brazil and wider Latin America.

rules.name: BITSAdmin transfer into Public or ProgramData
rules.description: bitsadmin /transfer downloading into a world-writable staging directory, commonly seen in Brazilian banking-trojan loaders.

rules.name: ExtExport.exe run outside Internet Explorer directories
rules.description: ExtExport.exe is a signed Internet Explorer helper that Guildma/Astaroth intrusions copy beside a malicious DLL for side-loading. Running it from user-writable folders is anomalous.

rules.name: AutoIt interpreter executed from user-writable path
rules.description: AutoIt3.exe or a renamed copy executing from ProgramData, Public or AppData, a packaging style reported for Metamorfo/Casbaneiro and Mispadu campaigns.

rules.name: Windows Script Host running script from Public or ProgramData
rules.description: wscript or cscript executing .vbs/.vbe/.js from a world-writable staging folder, the loader style reported across LATAM banking trojans.

rules.name: mshta executing a script staged in Public or ProgramData
rules.description: mshta.exe launching a local .hta/.vbs/.js from a world-writable path, a Casbaneiro/Metamorfo-style stage.

rules.name: msiexec quiet install from a remote URL
rules.description: msiexec /i with an http(s) package in quiet mode, a delivery step shared by Metamorfo, Javali and Mekotio chains.

rules.name: MSBuild compiling a project from a user-writable folder
rules.description: MSBuild.exe building a .proj/.csproj/.xml located in Public, ProgramData or Temp, an inline-task technique reported for BBTok and related Latin American loaders.

rules.name: Squirrel Update.exe pulling from a remote URL
rules.description: Squirrel's Update.exe with --update, --download or --install against an http URL has been abused as a trusted-looking downloader (reported for Coyote). Legitimate Electron updaters also use it, so this is an audit signal.

rules.name: Internet shortcut dropped in the Startup folder
rules.description: A .url file created in the user Startup folder, a persistence style reported for Blind Eagle (APT-C-36) droppers.

rules.name: Remcos RAT registry configuration key
rules.description: Remcos stores its license and settings under HKCU\Software\Remcos-<id>. Remcos is a staple of Blind Eagle and many LATAM campaigns.

rules.name: Remcos keylogger data folder
rules.description: Remcos writes keystroke and screenshot data under %APPDATA%\remcos\.

rules.name: AsyncRAT-style logon task with highest privileges
rules.description: schtasks creating an on-logon, highest-run-level task pointing into AppData\Roaming, the persistence default of AsyncRAT builds used by Blind Eagle.

rules.name: Browser launched with an extension loaded from a user-writable path
rules.description: chrome/msedge started with --load-extension pointing into AppData, ProgramData or Public, a banking-trojan technique for on-page fraud reported for Mekotio/Grandoreiro.

rules.name: Scheduled task launching mshta against a remote URL
rules.description: schtasks /create whose action is mshta with an http(s) URL, a persistence pattern publicly attributed to BITTER and other South Asian groups.

rules.name: rekeywiz.exe run outside System32 (SideCopy side-loading)
rules.description: SideCopy has side-loaded DUser.dll through a copied Credential Backup and Restore Wizard (rekeywiz.exe). The binary has no business outside System32.

rules.name: mshta fetching content from a raw IPv4 URL
rules.description: mshta with an http URL whose host is a bare IPv4 address, the delivery style reported for Gamaredon, SideWinder and several South Asian clusters.

rules.name: hh.exe decompiling a CHM file
rules.description: hh.exe -decompile unpacks CHM content to disk; CHM lures are used by Kimsuky and by South Asian groups such as Patchwork.

rules.name: CHM opened from a user-writable path
rules.description: hh.exe opening a .chm from Downloads, Temp, AppData or Public. CHM lures were used by Kimsuky, Patchwork and others; manuals are also legitimate so this is low severity.

rules.name: Hancom Hangul (HWP) spawning a shell or script host
rules.description: hwp.exe starting cmd, PowerShell, a script host, mshta, rundll32 or regsvr32. Malicious HWP documents and EPS exploits are a signature Korean-language lure used by Kimsuky and ScarCruft.

rules.name: Ghostscript spawning a shell (Hangul EPS exploitation)
rules.description: gswin32c/gswin64c with a command interpreter child is the tail of Hangul EPS exploit chains reported against South Korean targets.

rules.name: Korean NPKI certificate folder being copied or archived
rules.description: A copy or archive command touching the NPKI certificate directory. Theft of NPKI signing certificates is documented for Kimsuky and Lazarus intrusions.

rules.name: regsvr32 loading an ESTsoft-lookalike DLL from ProgramData
rules.description: AppleSeed-style persistence registers a DLL under ProgramData\Software\ESTsoft, mimicking the Korean ALYac vendor. The real product lives in Program Files.

rules.name: Run key launching mshta against a remote URL
rules.description: Autostart value invoking mshta with an http URL, the BabyShark/Kimsuky persistence pattern.

rules.name: Unsigned ffmpeg.dll or d3dcompiler_47.dll in 3CXDesktopApp
rules.description: The 2023 3CX supply-chain compromise (attributed to DPRK actors) shipped trojanized ffmpeg.dll and d3dcompiler_47.dll inside the 3CXDesktopApp directory.

rules.name: Windows Sandbox launched with a user-supplied .wsb file
rules.description: WindowsSandbox.exe started on a .wsb configuration from a user-writable path. JPCERT/CC and others documented MirrorFace running malware inside Windows Sandbox to evade host AV.

rules.name: Ichitaro word processor spawning a shell or script host
rules.description: JustSystems Ichitaro is a Japan-specific document target; a shell or script host child is a classic exploit tail. Vendor binary names are from public reporting and not verified here.

rules.name: WPS Office spawning a shell or script host
rules.description: Kingsoft WPS Writer/Spreadsheets/Presentation starting a shell, script host or LOLBin. WPS exploits have been used against Chinese-speaking and East Asian targets.

rules.name: Sunlogin client spawning a shell (RCE tail)
rules.description: SunloginClient.exe with a shell or PowerShell child matches exploitation of the widely abused Sunlogin remote-control RCE flaws.

rules.name: frp reverse-proxy client with a config file
rules.description: frpc/frps started with an ini or toml config, a Go reverse proxy used by many China-nexus groups. Also used by self-hosters, hence medium.

rules.name: nps/npc tunnel client with server and verify key
rules.description: npc started with -server= and -vkey=, the nps intranet-penetration client frequently seen in Chinese-language intrusion toolkits.

rules.name: fscan internal scanner invocation
rules.description: fscan, a Go all-in-one intranet scanner popular in Chinese-language red-team and intrusion toolkits, run with -h against an address range.

rules.name: ASPX written into Exchange OWA auth directory
rules.description: A .aspx created under FrontEnd\HttpProxy\owa\auth is the HAFNIUM/ProxyLogon web shell drop location documented by Microsoft and national CERTs.

rules.name: ASPX created in IIS aspnet_client
rules.description: Web shells dropped in inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client were a frequent HAFNIUM placement. Patching tools can touch the folder, so medium.

rules.name: Java application server child running recon commands
rules.description: java/tomcat spawning cmd or PowerShell with whoami, ipconfig or net user, the visible tail of JSP web shells (AntSword, Behinder, Godzilla) common in Chinese-language intrusions.

rules.name: Linux web server worker running recon shell commands
rules.description: php-fpm, httpd, nginx or apache2 parent running a shell with whoami, id, uname -a or reading /etc/passwd, the tail of PHP web shells (China Chopper, Behinder, Godzilla).

rules.name: Executable launched from ProgramData\SxS (PlugX staging)
rules.description: Binaries run from C:\ProgramData\SxS have been seen as PlugX side-loading staging. Heuristic from public write-ups; treat as an audit lead.

rules.name: Unsigned wsc.dll loaded outside Avast directories
rules.description: wsc.dll beside a renamed Avast wsc_proxy.exe is a repeatedly documented side-loading pair for Mustang Panda PlugX loaders.

rules.name: Unsigned libvlc.dll loaded outside VideoLAN directories
rules.description: A fake libvlc.dll next to a copied VLC binary is a recurring side-loading carrier for China-nexus loaders.

rules.name: Piriform Agomo registry values (CCleaner 5.33 backdoor)
rules.description: The 2017 CCleaner supply-chain compromise (APT17/Winnti-linked) wrote victim identifiers under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Piriform\Agomo (MUID, TID, NID). Historic but still a useful retro-hunt signal.

rules.name: Alibaba Cloud agent uninstall or kill on Linux
rules.description: Cryptominer and botnet operators (Rocke, TeamTNT lineage, many Chinese-language clusters) remove Alibaba Cloud security agents (aegis/aliyun) before deploying payloads.

rules.name: Tencent Cloud agent uninstall on Linux
rules.description: Removal of the Tencent Cloud monitoring stack (qcloud stargate/YunJing/BaradAgent), a defence-evasion step in Chinese-language cryptojacking tooling.

rules.name: COATHANGER FortiGate implant paths
rules.description: Files under a .bd.key directory (preload.so) are the persistence artefacts of COATHANGER, reported by Dutch MIVD/NCSC-NL against FortiGate devices.

rules.name: Pygmy Goat libsophos.so on a Sophos firewall
rules.description: NCSC UK published a malware analysis report on Pygmy Goat, a Linux SSH-style backdoor named libsophos.so deployed on Sophos XG firewalls.

rules.name: BPFDoor staging file in /dev/shm
rules.description: BPFDoor (Red Menshen, targeting telecoms in Asia and the Middle East) runs from /dev/shm/kdmtmpflush.

rules.name: BPFDoor lock and pid files
rules.description: BPFDoor variants create /var/run/haldrund.pid or /var/run/kdevrund.pid (and an initd.lock) as run markers.

rules.name: GotoHTTP remote-access tool executed
rules.description: GotoHTTP is a Chinese-origin web remote-control tool; its use on servers has been reported in Chinese-language intrusions. Legitimate use exists.

rules.name: rundll32 loading perfc.dat (NotPetya)
rules.description: NotPetya launches its payload with rundll32 C:\Windows\perfc.dat,#1. The file name is a stable public indicator of the 2017 Ukraine-origin wiper.

rules.name: perfc.dat written to the Windows directory
rules.description: NotPetya drops its DLL as C:\Windows\perfc.dat.

rules.name: schtasks scheduling a forced reboot as SYSTEM
rules.description: NotPetya schedules shutdown.exe /r /f via a one-shot SYSTEM task to trigger its MBR payload.

rules.name: Clearing Setup, System, Security and Application logs in one command
rules.description: NotPetya chains wevtutil cl across Setup, System, Security and Application. All four in one command is a strong destructive-run signal.

positive.command: wevtutil cl Setup & wevtutil cl System & wevtutil cl Security & wevtutil cl Application

rules.name: AdvancedRun used to stop Windows Defender
rules.description: WhisperGate stage two drops AdvancedRun.exe to run sc.exe stop WinDefend (CISA/FBI AA22-057A, Microsoft).

rules.name: Stage download named Tbopbh.jpg (WhisperGate)
rules.description: WhisperGate stage one fetches stage two disguised as Tbopbh.jpg from a Discord CDN path.

rules.name: HermeticWiper partition driver dropped
rules.description: HermeticWiper drops a signed EaseUS partition-manager driver (epmntdrv.sys, also spelled empntdrv.sys) to reach raw disk.

rules.name: caddy.exe executed from Temp or Windows directory
rules.description: CaddyWiper was deployed as caddy.exe, often via GPO (ESET, CISA AA22-057A). Name-based and easy to evade, hence medium.

rules.name: WinRAR archiving with delete and store flags (RoarBat-style wiping)
rules.description: Sandworm's RoarBat wipes by archiving with rar using -df/-dr and -m0 without a useful archive. The combination across directories is destructive.

rules.name: dd writing to MTD flash block devices (AcidRain)
rules.description: AcidRain, used against Viasat modems in Ukraine (2022), wipes /dev/mtdblock*, /dev/mtd* and similar device nodes.

rules.name: Executable launched directly from a NETLOGON or SYSVOL share
rules.description: Binaries run straight from NETLOGON or SYSVOL were used to mass-deploy wipers and ransomware (Industroyer2 era, Agrius, CaddyWiper). Logon scripts also live there, so low.

rules.name: Command line contacting free webhook or mock-API services
rules.description: curl/PowerShell reaching webhook.site, mocky.io, mockbin.org or pipedream.net. CERT-UA and others documented APT28 using these as free relays. Developers use them too, so low.

rules.name: Script contacting the Telegram Bot API
rules.description: PowerShell, curl or a script host reaching api.telegram.org/bot... is a C2 and exfiltration channel used by Dark Pink (SE Asia), Konni, and Ukraine-focused clusters.

rules.name: Volunteer or hacktivist DDoS tooling (mhddos, db1000n)
rules.description: Command lines for mhddos, db1000n or similar scripted DDoS tools used by both sides of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Low: it may be sanctioned in some contexts.

rules.name: Ammyy Admin remote tool executed
rules.description: Ammyy Admin was widely abused by Russian-speaking financial-crime crews (Cobalt, Silence, Buhtrap).

rules.name: Radmin Server silent install
rules.description: r_server.exe /silence or /install registers the Russian-origin Radmin Server unattended. Abused for persistent hands-on access.

rules.name: Remote Utilities (rutserv) running from a user-writable path
rules.description: RMS/Remote Utilities host (rutserv.exe) from Temp, AppData or ProgramData. Reported with Iranian (MuddyWater) and Eastern European intrusions.

rules.name: LiteManager server running from a user-writable path
rules.description: romserver.exe or romfusclient.exe outside Program Files. LiteManager is a Russian-origin tool seen in financial-crime intrusions; legitimate admin use exists.

rules.name: Shamoon RawDisk driver (drdisk.sys)
rules.description: Shamoon 2/3 wipers load the EldoS RawDisk driver as drdisk.sys from System32 (Saudi and wider Gulf campaigns).

rules.name: Service ImagePath pointing at trksvr.exe or ntssrv.exe
rules.description: Shamoon 1 masquerades as the Distributed Link Tracking service via trksvr.exe; Shamoon 2 used NtsSrv/ntssrv.exe. Genuine TrkSvr runs under svchost.

rules.name: EldoS RawDisk driver (ZeroCleare)
rules.description: ZeroCleare pairs a vulnerable VirtualBox driver with the EldoS RawDisk driver (elrawdsk.sys) for destructive disk access (IBM X-Force, Gulf energy sector).

rules.name: DiskCryptor driver (dcrypt.sys) written outside Program Files
rules.description: Moses Staff (Iran-linked, Israeli targets) deployed DiskCryptor via PyDCrypt/DCSrv, dropping dcrypt.sys.

rules.name: DarkComet keylogger data directory
rules.description: DarkComet writes captured data under %APPDATA%\dclogs\. The RAT has long been used in Middle East espionage and conflict-related campaigns.

rules.name: DarkComet DC3_FEXEC registry value
rules.description: DarkComet stores its persistence marker under HKCU\Software\DC3_FEXEC.

rules.name: netsh firewall allowedprogram for a user-writable binary (njRAT)
rules.description: njRAT punches a firewall hole with netsh firewall add allowedprogram. Heavily used across the Middle East and North Africa.

rules.name: njRAT keylogger registry value [kl]
rules.description: njRAT keeps keystroke data in a [kl] value under a 32-hex key in HKCU\Software.

rules.name: IIS native module installed via appcmd
rules.description: appcmd install module registers an IIS module. Malicious modules (RGDoor by OilRig, IISpy, others) are a way to persist in Middle East government hosting.

rules.name: plink/ssh reverse tunnel to local RDP
rules.description: A reverse SSH tunnel carrying 3389, a hallmark of Fox Kitten (Iran-nexus) access to VPN-connected hosts per CISA/FBI advisories.

rules.name: Atera agent MSI installed with integrator login
rules.description: msiexec with IntegratorLogin=/CompanyId= silently enrols the host into an attacker Atera tenant, reported by CISA for Iran-nexus and criminal actors.

rules.name: ScreenConnect client running outside its install directory
rules.description: ScreenConnect (ConnectWise) client binaries from user-writable paths, a technique documented for MuddyWater and criminal intrusion sets. Managed-service use is common, so low.

rules.name: SimpleHelp remote-access client from JWrapper
rules.description: JWrapper-Remote Access (SimpleHelp) executables in ProgramData or user paths. Abused by Iran-nexus and ransomware actors; MSP use is legitimate, so low.

rules.name: AnyDesk silent install with unattended access
rules.description: AnyDesk --install with --silent and --start-with-win or --set-password configures unattended access, a pre-ransomware step reported across regions.

rules.name: NetSupport Manager client from user-writable path
rules.description: client32.exe beside NSM.lic or client32.ini in AppData/ProgramData/Temp, used by NetSupport RAT campaigns.

rules.name: BitLocker protector added with recovery password on a data volume
rules.description: manage-bde adding recovery-password protectors and enabling encryption was reported by CISA in Iran-nexus ransomware cooperation. Admin and MDM use is common, so low.

rules.name: Agent Tesla style task from a temp XML
rules.description: schtasks /Create /TN "Updates\<name>" /XML tmp<hex>.tmp from %TEMP% is the Agent Tesla persistence routine. Agent Tesla, NanoCore and LokiBot are the long-running West African BEC toolset.

rules.name: NanoCore run.dat or catalog.dat in a GUID folder
rules.description: NanoCore keeps run.dat and catalog.dat under %APPDATA%\<GUID>\.

rules.name: NanoCore monitor-style scheduled task names
rules.description: NanoCore commonly registers tasks named like DHCP Monitor, UPnP Monitor, WAN Monitor, NTFS Subsystem or SMTP Service from user-writable binaries.

rules.name: LokiBot .lck/.hdb/.kdb files in AppData
rules.description: LokiBot creates six-hex-character folders with .lck, .hdb and .kdb files under %APPDATA% for locking and credential cache.

rules.name: NetWire registry configuration key
rules.description: NetWire RAT stores configuration under HKCU\Software\NetWire. A Nigerian-linked BEC staple.

rules.name: Injection-target .NET binary launched by a user-writable parent
rules.description: RegAsm, RegSvcs, MSBuild, InstallUtil, vbc or jsc spawned by a process in AppData, ProgramData, Public or Temp, the hollowing pattern of Agent Tesla, FormBook and NanoCore loaders.

rules.name: Clop ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Clop ransom note file name(s) ClopReadMe.txt. Clop operators are Russian-speaking and avoid CIS systems; victims span NA and EU file-transfer-appliance customers.

rules.name: Cuba ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Cuba ransom note file name(s) !!FAQ for Decryption!!.txt. Cuba ransomware has mostly hit the Americas and Europe (CISA AA22-335A).

rules.name: Ryuk ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Ryuk ransom note file name(s) RyukReadMe.txt, RyukReadMe.html. Ryuk (Russian-speaking Wizard Spider) targeted NA and European healthcare and enterprise.

rules.name: Babuk ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Babuk ransom note file name(s) How To Restore Your Files.txt. Babuk's leaked builder has spawned many regional variants, including ESXi lockers.

rules.name: LockBit 3.0 ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the LockBit 3.0 ransom note file name(s) Restore-My-Files.txt. LockBit is the most prolific RaaS; CERT-JP, ACSC and others published advisories on it.

rules.name: ALPHV/BlackCat ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the ALPHV ransom note file name(s) RECOVER-FILES.txt. Rust-based RaaS; observed in the Americas, Europe and APAC.

rules.name: Medusa ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Medusa ransom note file name(s) !!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt. Medusa has hit organisations worldwide including Latin America and Europe.

rules.name: Rhysida ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Rhysida ransom note file name(s) CriticalBreachDetected.pdf. Rhysida incidents include the 2023 Chilean Army breach and European public bodies (CISA AA23-319A).

rules.name: BlackByte ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the BlackByte ransom note file name(s) BlackByte_restoremyfiles.hta. BlackByte reuses ProxyShell-era access; victims in NA, EU and APAC.

rules.name: Akira ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Akira ransom note file name(s) akira_readme.txt. CERT-In issued a July 2023 advisory on Akira for Windows and Linux/ESXi.

rules.name: Trigona ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Trigona ransom note file name(s) how_to_decrypt.hta. Trigona victims are reported across Latin America, Europe and APAC.

rules.name: Phobos/8Base/Dharma ransom note
rules.description: Creation of the Phobos ransom note file name(s) info.hta. Phobos-family lockers (also 8Base, Dharma) hit small organisations globally with RDP-led access.

rules.name: REvil/Sodinokibi ransom note
rules.description: REvil: a random-prefixed -readme.txt note. REvil deliberately skips CIS keyboard layouts, a documented Russian-speaking regional tell.

rules.name: Black Basta wallpaper and icon resources
rules.description: Black Basta drops dlaksjdoiwq.jpg and fkdjsadasd.ico in the temp directory as wallpaper and file icon. Victims concentrated in Europe and NA.

rules.name: Prestige ransom note in Public
rules.description: Prestige (attributed to Sandworm, aimed at Ukraine and Polish logistics in 2022) drops a note named README in C:\Users\Public.

rules.name: Prestige .enc file association
rules.description: Prestige registers a .enc extension under HKCR with an icon pointing to its note resources.

rules.name: fsutil symlink evaluation enabled (ALPHV hallmark)
rules.description: ALPHV/BlackCat enables remote-to-remote and remote-to-local symlink evaluation with fsutil to reach network shares.

rules.name: LanmanServer MaxMpxCt raised (ALPHV hallmark)
rules.description: ALPHV sets MaxMpxCt to 65535 for faster parallel SMB encryption.

rules.name: Royal/BlackSuit locker invocation with -path and -id
rules.description: Royal ransomware (royal_w.exe) takes -path and a 32-hex -id argument (CISA AA23-061A).

rules.name: Shadow copies removed via WMI object (Akira)
rules.description: Akira removes shadow copies with PowerShell Get-WmiObject Win32_Shadowcopy | Remove-WmiObject (CERT-In advisory).

rules.name: vssadmin shrinking shadow storage
rules.description: vssadmin resize shadowstorage to a tiny maxsize forces shadow copy deletion, used by Conti, Ryuk, Maze and Mallox lineages.

rules.name: ESXi forced VM process kill
rules.description: esxcli vm process kill --type=force, used by Akira, Royal, Black Basta and ALPHV Linux lockers to release VMDK locks.

rules.name: Ebury (Windigo) trojanized library names
rules.description: Ebury replaces or adds libns2/libns5/libpw3 style shared objects in /lib64 or /lib (ESET). It targets hosting providers in Europe and worldwide.

rules.name: regsvr32 registering a DLL from Public or ProgramData
rules.description: regsvr32 /s loading a DLL staged in a world-writable directory, a loader step reported for Grandoreiro and Mekotio chains in Latin America and Spain.

rules.name: certutil decoding a staged file in Public or ProgramData
rules.description: certutil -decode/-decodehex into a world-writable folder, seen in Brazilian banking-trojan droppers.

rules.name: UltraViewer running from a user-writable path
rules.description: UltraViewer, a Vietnam-origin remote-support tool, is abused in scams and intrusions. Legitimate helpdesk use is common, so low.

rules.name: attrib hiding folders on removable-drive paths
rules.description: attrib +h +s on a drive-root folder is the USB-lure technique reported for Mustang Panda and Gamaredon (hide real files, show a shortcut).

rules.name: cmd launching mshta with a remote URL from a shortcut-style parent
rules.description: cmd /c start of mshta http..., the Kimsuky/Konni LNK follow-on step. Broad on its own, so keyed on cmd.exe plus mshta plus URL.

rules.name: wscript running a VBS from Temp with a hidden window switch
rules.description: wscript //B or //E:vbscript on a Temp script is the loader style of H-Worm/Houdini and other Middle East commodity RAT campaigns.

rules.name: Office launched with a remote template URL
rules.description: winword started with an http template argument; remote-template injection is a Gamaredon staple against Ukrainian organisations.

rules.name: Linux wiper pattern: shred or dd over many disks
rules.description: shred -n/-z against /dev/sd* devices, a destructive pattern shared by Linux wipers used in the Russia-Ukraine theatre (for example AcidRain relatives and RedAlert variants).

rules.name: chattr used on cloud agent directories
rules.description: chattr -i or +i on Alibaba/Tencent agent folders, used by Chinese-language miner kits to lock or unlock agent files around removal.

rules.name: PowerShell invoking mshta against a remote URL
rules.description: powershell starting mshta with an http URL, a MuddyWater and OilRig-era chain step.
